Scenario Config Editor

Build a training scenario one section at a time. Your edits stay in this browser until you download them.

Load or import a scenario package to begin.
✦

Start with a scenario package

Load the shipped examples to explore how instructor settings shape the student’s training experience, or import a package you already have.

SECTION 01

Basics

Identify this scenario in the package and in the student’s scenario menu. These values do not change the facility layout.

Changing the scenario ID updates its manifest entry and downloaded filename. Unity checks facility and catalog compatibility when the package is launched.

SECTION 02

Network Training

Set the network rules, device roles, and evidence students use to complete the lab. Per-student addresses, VLAN assignments, and credentials may be generated during the training run.

SECTION 03

Facility & Equipment

Describe the equipment available, rack and endpoint placements students must complete, and the cabling relationships used by the lab. IDs must refer to items Unity knows about.

SECTION 04

Binder Content

Edit the seven student-facing reference sections. Text may include supported tokens such as {ScenarioId} and {Ssid}; the preview below resolves instructor-authored values.

LIVE PREVIEW

Student binder preview

Preview updates as you edit. Runtime-generated values remain placeholders when the browser does not know them.

SECTION 05

Review & Export

Check package structure and scenario consistency, then download the updated files. Browser validation helps catch authoring issues; Unity remains the final authority for facility compatibility and launch validation.

Package checks

These checks do not replace Unity validation.

Download files

Export the scenario JSON and matching manifest, then place them in the scenario package.

SECTION 06

Advanced JSON

Inspect or edit the complete scenario document. Use this when working with fields not covered by the guided forms. Valid JSON edits sync back to the other sections; incomplete JSON is held until it can be parsed.

Drafts are saved in this browser.Unity is the final package validator.
